title: Quran Study from Parivash 40: Sura 3:59–80 (1989-12-29)
document_summary: Catherine leads a study of Quran 3:59–80. Jesus is compared with Adam, and participants ask whether messengers themselves can experience doubt and need reassurance. The logical agreement with Jews and Christians is worship of God alone, while disputes over Muhammad, Jesus, Mary, Mosaic law, or Christian law are treated as ego and human factors. The group urges rigorous self-examination by beginning with the possibility that one remains an idolater. Christian outreach, John 20:17, the Nicene Creed, the people of the cave, and the political formation of the Trinity receive extended attention. The closing verses condemn twisting scripture and state that no prophet or messenger would command people to worship him or angels instead of God.

related_duplicate_sources.note: The audio gives a Quran-study setting.

related_duplicate_sources.relationship: same one-religion and Jewish-Christian salvation discussion
related_duplicate_sources.note: The present source emphasizes God-alone agreement.
The audio contains Catherine's more cautious exposition.

content_guidance.instruction: Do not flatten the study into Rashad's polemic.

content_guidance.rule: Separate Quranic exegesis from Christian history
content_guidance.instruction: Use independent sources for historical claims.

content_guidance.rule: Do not accuse users of idolatry
content_guidance.instruction: Present the self-audit as the speakers' teaching.

sections.title: The logical agreement with Jews and Christians, God alone, Abrahamic religion, and human ego
sections.summary: Quran 3:64 calls scripture communities to worship God alone without human lords. Rashad says Christians and Jews reject the proposal because of ego and social ties to Jesus, Muhammad, Mary, or inherited identity. The community's practices are traced to Abraham rather than Mosaic or later Christian law.

sections.title: John 20:17, the Nicene Creed, the Trinity, political power, and the people of the cave
sections.summary: The group cites Jesus' statement 'my God and your God' against the Trinity. Matt discusses the Council of Nicaea, and Rashad says a political minority imposed Trinitarian doctrine in 325 CE while dissenters included the people of the cave.
related_questions: How did the group describe Nicaea?

sections.canonical_text: Dr. Khalifa: This reminds me, confounding the truth with falsehood. This is typical of any Christian missionary or preacher or somebody who comes to your house trying to convert you to Christianity. We were visiting the great Karmallys, in Vancouver. This is Feroz and Batool Karmally sitting there in the corner.
